evidence.note: Opens on the thesis: 'A shared rooftop array could undercut what blocks C and D pay for daytime power'.
'About 40% of what flats on blocks C and D spend on electricity falls in daylight hours' grounds the thesis in the size of the daytime spend.
'26 of the 33 households that answered the survey support a pilot' adds resident demand and introduces the pilot.
'A 12-month pilot tests savings and upkeep on two roofs first' states the proposal that follows from that support.
'One shared array per roof feeds the block's landlord supply' explains how the pilot delivers the saving.
'Roof leaks, falling tariffs and later upkeep are the pilot's main risks' gives the counter-case before the ask.
'The board is asked to approve the £86,400 pilot, with a go or stop review at twelve months' closes with the decision; the 12-month review echoes s-4 but as the ask, not a repeat finding.

rationale: The titles state findings throughout, with the thesis on the first slide, and run in order from opportunity to evidence of need and support, then proposal, mechanism, risks and ask. Each title connects to its neighbour with no contradiction or repeated finding; the s-7 restatement of the review turns it into the decision. Read alone, the titles summarise the pitch, which matches the pass descriptor.
